- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and add a slight downward slope to reflect momentum decay.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model often underestimates upward momentum — increase forecast by 2-5% for next 3-5 days to capture sentiment-driven rally.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1-3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile — add 1-3% buffer to short-term forecast if sentiment swings >0.3.  
- When sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model often fails to recognize reversal — delay peak forecast by 1-2 days and increase slope gently to reflect sentiment lag.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate volatility — smooth out extreme swings and anchor to 3-5 day moving average of recent history to avoid overfitting to sentiment noise.
